transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (CSM), Samir (SE); Laura (Ironbark VP Eng), Daniel (Head ML), Priya (Security), Omar (SRE)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align stakeholders for a 6-week pilot: clarify environment (VPC vs hosted), security needs (SAML, KMS, SOC2), performance targets (p50/p95 latency, QPS), and immediate action items for pilot provisioning. Ran through a high-level implementation plan and sequencing for network, creds, and evals.

Topics: pilot scope, network connectivity, security/compliance, success criteria, timeline, next steps

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick round of intros?
[00:12] Laura: hi this is laura, vp eng at ironbark, we own platform and infra and i'll be sponsor for this pilot
[00:18] Daniel: daniel here, head of ml, i'll be working with samir on evals and perf
[00:23] Priya: priya, security architect, i'll be owning the compliance checklist and risk sign-off
[00:28] Omar: omar, sre, i'll handle network and peering with you guys
[00:33] Maya: and i'm maya ae at redwood, with ethan our csm and samir our se. goal for today is to get a crisp plan to stand up the pilot and unblock network/security

[02:05] Ethan: quick note on timeline we typically see pilot cadence over 4-6 weeks for a VPC or private deployment, hosted can be faster but given your compliance ask we expect VPC/private discussion

[03:10] Samir: to clarify terminology — Redwood Private is customer-managed control plane option vs Redwood Dedicated reserved GPU pools vs Hosted API. sometimes the auto-transcribe drops words, so i'll say 'private control plane' and 'dedicated capacity' just to avoid confusion

[04:00] Daniel: our priority is latency for customer-facing assistant. target p95 under 450ms for short prompts, p50 under 180ms. throughput about 10 qps steady with spikes to 30 qps. cost is... important but performance first for 1.0

[04:35] Maya: good detail. we'll capture those as pilot success criteria. Ethan, i'll flag that we should bake those into the KPI doc

[05:12] Priya: on security we're SOC 2 required, strict key management — we prefer bring-your-own-KMS (BYO KMS) and need audit logs and SSO via SAML. are those supported in the private/on-prem flow?

[05:36] Samir: yes, the private offering supports customer KMS integration and SAML SSO. audit logs and longer retention are available as an add-on. small caveat: for on-prem some of the observability hooks are agent-based and require a small collector to run in your cluster

[06:20] Omar: on networking, we want direct peering, not broad internet egress. does redwood support VPC peering and private link?

[06:32] Ethan: we do support VPC peering and private link. i'll follow up with the peering checklist and sample routing tables. samir will provide the exact ports and cidr ranges

[07:10] Samir: yeah i'll share a network diagram. note though, if you choose Hosted with strict egress via private link there are additional controls but some latency implications. Dedicated in-region tends to be the middle ground for predictability

[08:02] Laura: curious about model hosting. we have an internal safety filter and want to keep PII out of vendor logs. can we set retention to zero and opt-out of telemetry?

[08:23] Maya: option to disable telemetry and set zero retention exists for Private deployments; for Hosted we can anonymize and set retention windows per contract. we'll include a telemetry/retention section in the security pack

[09:10] Daniel: regarding models, are you onboarding our finetuned models or does redwood host model variants? performance differences between quantized and fp16? we've seen quantized models shave 30-40% cost but some quality delta

[09:34] Samir: we support both; for pilot we usually recommend a small A/B: one quantized variant and one full precision to compare latency/quality. we can automate routing fallback to the higher-quality model if outputs fail quality checks

[10:12] Priya: does redwood provide eval tooling or do we need to bring our own test harness?

[10:22] Ethan: Redwood Optimize has eval integrations; samir can demo a lightweight harness that runs your prompt set and tracks regressions. we'll also export metrics to your prometheus if you want

[11:05] Omar: how do we surface cost visibility per route? we need token-level cost mapping to our billing center

[11:20] Maya: console provides per-route and token breakdown with tags, and we can push billing reports to your billing S3. for Dedicated we can provide more granular breakdown and reserved capacity amortization

[12:00] Daniel: pilot data — we'll share a 2k prompt sample and expected QPS matrix. also want to test prompt prefix caching and KV cache performance for chat sessions

[12:20] Samir: note on phrasing — prefix caching (auto prefix/K V cache) will help a ton with multi-turn. sometimes transcripts call it 'K V cash' so just calling it the KV cache here

[13:30] Laura: who will be the day-to-day contact? we want one owner from redwood and a technical SE contact for blockers

[13:45] Maya: Ethan will be your CSM and day-to-day owner; Samir is technical lead for the pilot; i'll coordinate contractual and exec touchpoints

[14:50] Ethan: ok next up, onboarding steps. step 1: security review and SOC2 docs. step 2: network peering and subnet whitelisting. step 3: staging provisioning and API keys. step 4: run perf evals and model comparisons. step 5: adjust config (batching, quantization) and iterate

[16:10] Priya: on SOC2, can you provide a letter of attestation and details on encryption at rest (KMS)? also we need to check data residency — we're required to keep data in US-EAST region for now

[16:35] Samir: we can provide SOC2 snapshot, KMS integration docs, and region pinning for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has region options but with some limitations on isolation unless you go Dedicated

[17:20] Daniel: about metrics — will we get token-level latency and model internal traces? we want to correlate user latency with model seq length and cold-start events

[17:40] Samir: yes, console tracing provides per-request latency, seq-length breakdown, and KV hit rates. cold-start is rare with persistent workers but we'll instrument for your traffic pattern and show warmup guidance

[19:05] Omar: any firewall or NAT traversal issues we should be aware of when peering to your endpoints? we run strict egress rules

[19:26] Samir: you'll need to open outbound to a small set of IPs when using private link; for VPC peering it's direct and simpler but requires route table changes. i'll put exact firewall rules in the network checklist

[21:00] Laura: success criteria — we'll propose: p95 < 450ms on short prompts, latency SLA 99.9% availability for pilot windows, model accuracy > baseline (TBD), cost per 1k tokens under internal target. can we formalize that?

[21:25] Maya: absolutely, we'll draft a pilot KPI doc and share it. Ethan will own the doc and invite you to iterate

[22:10] Daniel: timeline — aiming to start pilot traffic week of 2/23 and run for 4 weeks. any blockers?

[22:20] Priya: need to review SOC2 docs before starting and confirm KMS mapping; otherwise ok

[22:35] Omar: show me the peering diagram and we'll replicate in staging once i have the cidrs

[24:00] Samir: i'll send the peering diagram and a small runbook for bringing up the staging environment. note: if you want on-prem package, there's slightly longer lead time for installation and cert signing

[25:15] Laura: what's the typical time to provision a dedicated pool vs private?

[25:30] Ethan: Dedicated in-region is 3-7 days typically once contract is signed, private control plane depends on your infra but pilot on a VPC peering path can be done in 1-2 weeks if networking approvals move quickly

[26:10] Daniel: curious about rollback strategies — if model upgrade causes quality regression can we auto-fail to previous model?

[26:23] Samir: yes, rollouts include canary and automatic fallback. you can pin traffic percentages and set automatic rollback on eval regression rules

[27:40] Priya: any penetration test requirements? we may need to include redwood in our vendor pentest scope

[27:50] Maya: we provide an environment for pen testing with limited-data stubs and we can coordinate a tacit nda and scoping call. i'll add legal/procurement touchpoint

[28:30] Omar: metrics export — can we push traces to our prometheus and logs to our splunk?

[28:45] Samir: yes, we have exporters for prometheus and options for log forwarding to Splunk or S3. some connectors are part of the observability add-on

[30:10] Ethan: ok recap of concrete action items: maya to send security pack, samir to send peering diagram & firewall rules, ethan to set up pilot in console and share API keys, daniel to provide prompts and qps, priya to review SOC2 and KMS mapping

[31:00] Laura: can you also include a simple cost estimate for running the pilot (2 models, 10 qps average) so we can run it by finance?

[31:15] Maya: yes we'll give a conservative estimate and two scenarios: hosted vs dedicated vs private. note: dedicated amortizes reserved capacity which changes unit economics

[32:40] Daniel: one more thing — we have an internal request to test data anonymization at ingestion. is there a recommended pattern?

[32:55] Samir: yes, the recommended approach is client-side tokenization/anonymization before sending to the model, plus masking in the logs. we can show a small middleware example in node/python

[34:10] Priya: SSO — we need SAML and role-based access controls, especially around who can view PII in logs

[34:30] Ethan: SAML with SCIM provisioning and RBAC mapping is supported. we'll include a runbook for group mapping

[36:00] Omar: any quotas or throttling we should be aware of for the staging api keys?

[36:12] Samir: staging keys come with configurable rate limits; we'll set them conservatively for the pilot and adjust once we see real traffic

[37:40] Laura: ok sounds good — anything on legal or procurement we need to do ahead of pilot?

[37:52] Maya: procurement will want the standard SLA and security appendix; i'll loop in our legal, but it's not a blocker to start staging work. contracting for Dedicated or Private usually takes longer

[39:10] Daniel: i'm excited to compare quantized variant vs fp16 on our prompts. let's make sure to include a blind eval so bias creeps aren't obvious

[40:00] Samir: yep, we'll set up blinded A/B eval and surface quality metrics. we'll also track KV hit rate and latency breakdown by seq len

[41:20] Ethan: scheduling note — i'll send a calendar invite for the network deep dive (Samir, Omar) and a separate date for the SE perf run (Samir, Daniel)

[42:05] Priya: any specific encryption-in-transit concerns? we run strict TLS policies and mutual TLS is preferred for some endpoints

[42:20] Samir: mutual TLS is supported for private link; we'll include cert rotation guidance in the runbook

[43:55] Maya: alright final recap — next steps and owners captured. can we get a thumbs up on timeline to start pilot week of 2/23?

[44:10] Laura: yes that's our target as long as SOC2 review goes quickly
[44:18] Priya: we'll try to turn SOC2 review around by 2/18
[44:25] Omar: i'll aim to have cidrs and initial firewall changes by 2026-02-17
[44:33] Daniel: i'll upload the prompt set and usage matrix by 2026-02-18

[45:00] Maya: perfect — thanks everyone. ethan will recap in an email with the pilot KPI doc and all action items. we'll follow up on the network deep dive invite
[45:20] Ethan: thanks all. we'll share links: security pack, network checklist, and pilot onboarding doc in the next 24 hours
[45:40] Maya: thanks, bye everyone

End of transcript
